newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rato says taxes won't rise for 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato says taxes won't rise for 97 budget.

text.p: Spain's Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said the conservative government would not raise taxes to enable the 1997 budget to meet the requirements for Spain to join in Europe's single currency launch two year's later.
In an interview with Spanish radio station Cope, Rato said "There are no tax rises planned."
Rato, when asked how the government could manage to meet the rigid deficit requirements for the Euro's launch, said "With good management."
The 1997 budget must be presented by the end of the month.
Rato said that far from raising taxes overall, income taxes would be deflated to take inflation into account.
Nonetheless, Rato did not rule out applying a fee on public health prescriptions.
"If a fee is applied, it won't cost the chronically ill and pensioners will have some benefits," Rato said.
But he repeated that the budget would be "complicated", although he said that the ministries were following instructions to cut expenditures.
"Not only are the instructions perfectly clear, but the ministries share (these views)," Rato said.
He declined to give any hint of the fundamental guidelines of the budget, saying the "process of putting the budget together requires a final decision on measures."
